subject.title: feat: add config option to suppress untrusted metadata blocks in Discord chat display

question: Should Discord hide OpenClaw-injected inbound metadata blocks by default using the existing display sanitizer, or should maintainers accept a new Discord config option for metadata visibility?
rationale: The code already defines these blocks as non-display metadata, while the requested solution adds a new config surface that root policy says needs a high bar and maintainer intent.

options.title: Hide by default
options.body: Fix any Discord-visible leak by applying the existing metadata-display sanitizer at the appropriate visible-output boundary and avoid a new config key.

options.title: Add Discord config
options.body: Introduce a documented `channels.discord` visibility option with clear default, upgrade behavior, and focused tests.

options.title: Defer product change
options.body: Keep the issue open until a live Discord proof shows which visible path still leaks metadata and whether current sanitizers already cover it.

recommendation.title: Hide by default
recommendation.body: Fix any Discord-visible leak by applying the existing metadata-display sanitizer at the appropriate visible-output boundary and avoid a new config key.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implicated lines all trace to Vincent Koc's recent refactor commit, with adjacent history from Peter Steinberger.
